task_prompt: Is it important to care about climate change?
response_text:
It is absolutely imperative to care about climate change because of its many negative effects. Climate change and global warming will cause plants and animals to go extinct, widespread glacier melting and stronger, more frequent natural disasters. This will result in many deaths, massive amounts of destruction and losses of entire ecosystems. Climate change is something we cannot possibly ignore. 

Firstly, due to warming temperatures, many plants and animals will die off. Many plants will not be able to live in the warmer climates as they are just not adapted to it. If plants in ecosystems die off, many herbivores that rely on those plants to live will also begin to go extinct as they have no food. The same goes with the carnivores - if the herbivores die, the carnivores will have no prey and die as well - leading to a collapse of an ecosystem. All thriving ecosystems are adapted to be able to live in their current climate, however if that climate changes, they won't have the ability to sustain themselves anymore. It is predicted that by 2050, nearly 50% all plants and animals may go extinct - a frightening number. 

Next, the globe warming up means bad news for the ice sheets covering the Arctic and Antarctica because warmer temperatures means faster melting. At the current melting rate, animals that rely on these glaciers to survive won't have much longer to live. Such an animal is the polar bear, who spends all winter on the ice sheets hunting for seals, and all summer on  broken ice waiting for winter. Soon, these polar bears will be spending their summer on broken ice and their winters swimming in freezing, open water. Another effect of the glaciers melting is that sea levels will rise. This might not seem terrible, however rising sea levels will result in many coastal cities to be permanently flooded, destroying billions of dollars of infrastructure and potentially killing millions. 

Finally, speaking of flooding, climate change has led to a large increase in natural disasters. Like I mentioned before, the melting of glaciers and rising sea levels will cause floods, but it will also result in much stronger storms. The more water from the glaciers plus the warmer temperatures is the perfect recipe for a hurricane. Over the past couple of years, the large storm rate has gone up and more hurricanes have touched down on land than before. Another disaster that is a result of climate change are droughts and famines. Especially common in dry countries such as the middle east where it is already very hot, the increasing temperatures will cause the little water they have to dry up and the crops to wilt. 

In conclusion, it is important to care about climate change for many reasons. It can cause mass extinction and many deaths, melt the glaciers causing sea levels to rise and massive damage and destruction due to an increase of natural disasters. This is why climate change cannot be ignored.

However, if someone lives in a constantly warm place, they would eventually run out of different ways to momentarily cool themselves off. There are limited things a person has available to them. An example of this is people using a fan to cool themselves off. The chances of having someone carry around a fan with them every single day is very limiting as to what a person can do, and it is simply unreasonable. With people not wanting to carry around extra items, sometimes they might like to simply remain warm throughout their day.

When a person is warm and starts sweating a lot, there are chances for them to lose something called water weight. If, for example, a person is already really skinny and they lose that extra water weight, there is a very slim chance that could lead to some serious health concerns in the future. Adding on to that, there are also the times when the person has to go out into both the sun and warm weather. If they do not have any way of cooling themselves off, they could sweat away a lot of the water weight they had.

Going outside in extremely warm/hot weather can result in heat strokes, especially if someone has to continuously work outside. Adding on to that, the heat being continuous can become very dangerous if someone does not take care of themselves properly. Things such as running common errands can become a problem, which can then cause a major disturbance in a schedule. Another problem that arises from going out is not having the proper protection against the sun and/or the heat. Developing rashes due to the heat, getting sun burns because of the sun, those are only a few of the many things that can make going outside not worth it.

Being in a living condition where it is constantly warm is not the most ideal living situation. Many common things such as going outside or, in extreme cases, finding cooling centres, becomes difficult.

To begin, if one were to observe teens, they would most likely observe that they always seem to be occupied in some sort of manner-they never seem to be idle! There are so many responsibilities and expectations that teenagers are constantly juggling with and trying to handle. This is why I believe that, due to posting on social media, attending highschool and completing homework, and working at their jobs, today's teens are too busy.

     For starters, many teenagers nowadays have some form of social media following and so therefore have to ensure that they regularly post to maintain their followers. A study found that "5 out of 8 teens have more than a thousand followers on any given social media platform". Considering that so many adolescents are influencers, and that for some, social media is even a source of income, it comes as no surprise that they have to spend up to hours per day creating, perfecting, and posting content. Unsurpisingly, teens find themselves loaded with more work and less time, becoming more and more busy as a result.

     Another reason why teens are so busy is because of highschool. They are required to attend school for six hours a day, and then come home to complete the pages upon pages of homework assigned by every teacher. Surveys show that "94% of highschoolers spend at least five hours after school doing schoolwork". Most students have around five hours of the day left after coming back from school, so having to spend at least this amount of time, if not more, on schoolwork, means that there really is not much time left over for other activities. However, there is much more to a teenager's life other than school, as mentioned above, and so, due to this reduction in the amount of time they have in a day, teenagers find themselves in an extremely busy lifestyle.

     Last but not least, many teenagers are expected to find part-time jobs when they turn 16, whether it be to build a better college application, contribute to college fees, or just start contributing to their families financially. Statistics indicate that "3 out of 5 adolescents work at least 10 hours per week". Devoting this much time to working, all while ensuring that they are attending school and keeping up-to-date with assignments and tests, puts too much on adolescents' plates. They therefore, once again, lead busy lives, trying to balance all of the various aspects that are associated with being a teen.

     In summary, teenagers have a lot of responsibilities and tasks in their daily lives, and, as everyone, feels, not enough time in the day to get everything done. There are obligations, expectations, and desires of others and themselves that they must answer to. This is why I believe that today's teens are too busy, as they have to regularly make social media posts, attend highschool and complete homework, and go to work at their part-time jobs.

Did you know that the plastic bag was once considered the greatest invention humans have achieved? a lot has changed in the past decade. Words like "climate change" appear daily in schools, workplaces, and the press. But is it really that important for us common civilian folk to care about it?

Many people disagree with me when I state this, but I have found the various methods used to influence environmentalism amongst students to be more irritant than encouraging.

Firstly, there has always been a degree of hypocrisy in the subject. In 2016, my elementary school back in China was promoting environmentalism and the fight against pollution in climate change. Throughout their power point presentation, they have stated many times to stay away from plastic products in general, especially plastic bags. But to make the subject fun for second graders like myself at the time, they decided to implement an activity for us to do. We were all given pots, soil, and seeds to grow at home for ourselves as growing plants does help with improving climate. But how were those equipment stored when they were brought to our classroom? Large, non-recyclable, plastic bags. Another example of hypocrisy would occur to me again in Canada with my high school geography teacher. She was heavily against the logging industries of Canada, all in the name of animals losing their habitats. But while she was talking about all this, the heels of her leather boots, her desk, the papers she was grading, the desks of all her students, the shelves and cabinets behind her, the frames for her photographs, were all made of wood. Her glasses were made of plastic. It is hard to be convinced by those who oppose their own opinions. Hypocrites.

Secondly, the method of introduction. Students aren't going to be fond of topics they get homework and tested on. I remember staying up way past my sleep schedule, to complete an 800 word essay about climate change. If my goal was to promote environmentalism, I would've introduced it in an amusing, rewarding fashion.  Rewards are always a better motivator than fear. To be convinced, people are gonna need a motivator, preferably of personal benefit.

Thirdly, effectiveness and importance. In this day and age Everyone has a closer matter to attend to compared to climate change. People are not going to waste time following the ways of environmentalism if that means more work. Climate change is here, but it's not pressing enough. Climate change doesn't disappear overnight after you decide to not use plastic for a day. The result is simply not immediate. People would rather focus on their own priorities rather than wild animals and there is no problem with that. We do not all share the same amount of compassion for things we are not related to. 

At the end, we are simply not bothered enough to view climate change as something important in our lives.

task_prompt: Is it important to care about climate change?
response_text:
It is very important to care about climate change. This is because climate change is affecting the health and safety of humans and other organisms in certain places, depleting numerous much-needed resources in various parts of the world, and that it is causing damages to infrastructures and habitats. Therefore, it's evident that climate change is detrimentally affecting many humans and other organisms around the world, making it an important cause to care about.

Climate change is affecting the health and safety of many organisms, including humans. For example, in some parts of China, the release of pollutant particles into the atmosphere has worsened the air quality, which, according to some studies, has increased the risk for residents of those regions to develop respiratory illnesses. Similarly, plastic and other waste objects that were released into oceans have trapped many marine creatures (e.g. sea turtles, etc), often causing injury or, in severe cases, death. These examples show that climate change has caused devastating consequences to the health and safety of many people and animals around the world.

Climate change is also decreasing the amount of resources available to humans. For example, due to climate change, droughts are becoming more common in parts of Africa. These droughts have made it more difficult to grow sufficient amounts of crops, resulting in an increased rate of hunger and malnourishment. Similar issues have been observed in parts of Central America, where floods have damaged aquatic plants that were supposed to be harvested. These issues are evidence that climate change is making it difficult for many people around the World to access essential resources that they need.

Additionally, climate change is causing damages to human infrastructures and organism habitats. For example, the floods that climate change has caused in Florida destroyed many near-ocean infrastructures  including homes. This has brought about massive economic losses, and forced many people to migrate or immigrate to a different location. Similarly, global warming, which results from the release of heat-trapping greenhouse gasses into the atmosphere, has caused icecaps to melt in the North Pole. This has affected polar bears and seals, whose habitats the melted icecaps were a vital part of. These examples show that climate change often causes massive property losses in different forms, and requires people and other organisms to take drastic measures (usually moving) to mitigate these losses.

In conclusion, climate change should be a cause to care about. This is because it has resulted in, and will continue to result in, damages to the health and safety of humans and other organisms, to much-needed resources, and to humans' and other organisms' infrastructures. These damages threaten many aspects (e.g. health, habitat availability, basic resources, etc) of all lives on earth. In fact, the sustainability and livability of our world in the future depends on awareness and mitigation of the effects of climate change.

task_prompt: Would you live in a place that is always warm?
response_text:
Would you rather live someplace cold, or somplace warm? After being faced with this question many times, my immediate response would always be cold, not because I enjoy it, but because I would not want to live somewhere warm. Years of living in Canada and the many trips visiting extended family in Mexico have made this question very easy to respond to. The weather, uncomfortable feeling, and the constant heat are some of the major factors in my decision.
       To start, the weather that the warm climate brings can be annoying. In the morning, it's nice and fresh, the sun is out and there are not many clouds in the sky only to be changed in the afternoon to a cloudy grey sky and very agressive rain. If there sky is still bright and blue with little clouds, the sun will ruin that. As soon as one steps into the sunlight, they would probably be able to instantly feel the warm. Staying oustide for long periods of time can make that warmth turn into something hotter and this heat will bring upon many things
       The uncomfortable feeling that heat brings is one of the things that makes it easy to believe that cold places are better. Because of the warm environment, sweating is going to be a daily thing that can not be stopped unless you have air conditiong. When that sweat starts to dry, many body parts such as hands and arms will start to get sticky and will make someone get the feeling of being musty or icky. Mosquitos are another problem. During the night, these animals will make it difficult to sleep because one will get consantly circled while they continously make buzzing sounds. The size of the ones I have encounted in Mexico are bigger than the ones I encountered here in Canada, making me fear them. I believe that the one cause for all of these problems is the constant heat.
       The constant heat makes things worse than I have already mentioned. The inside of the vehicle that people drive will turn into an oven. It can get so bad that it feels like the heat is suffocating.I'm sure that many people have already experienced this feeling but from what I have experienced, when comparing the two, the inside of a vehicle can be so much worse than here in Canada. This constant heat also made the bedroom so hot, we needed to leave the windows open, which let in the mosquitos. If it rained, the heat would make the hair moist, which makes it worse when paired up with this heat. It felt like the only place I would be protected from these things would be inside.
       The weather, and the uncomfortable feeling paired up with the constant heat make up for one mean experience. One could say that the only reason I put up with it is because my family makes Mexico fun. Hopefully it is not this bad next time. I will just have to wait and see.

task_prompt: Is it important to care about climate change?

There is concrete evidence that climate change is causing weather to be different, and in many cases, rougher. An example of this is many islands are sinking, or more so the ocean is rising. Oceans all around the world are rising because the ice caps are melting. Secondly, this issue was caused by humans. There have been spikes of temperature in the past but never in the Earth's history has the temperature changed so quickly and by so much. Many animals are struggling at this time such as the polar bears were. Habitats have been destroyed and the animals have nowhere to live. The animals did not have anything to do with it but they are also feeling the consquences of global warming. Finally, this issue is only resolvable by humans. Animals cannot solve this because they do not have the intelligence to do so. task_prompt: Is it important to care about climate change?
response_text:
Why is it important to talk about climate change? One of the biggest issues our planet faces today is climate change. Climate change is the warming of our earth. Climate change affects many things around us including the weather, the oceans and wildlife. climate change is an important issue we all should care about. 

Many animals have had to change their way of life because of it. An example of this are animals that live in cold places like polar bears, polar bears are used to extremely cold climates. Because the earth is warming up the cold climate that they are used to is also warming up, causing an entire species to change the way that they have lived. It is also causing ice to melt which forces polar bears to change the way they hunt, normally they would use the ice to hide and wait for prey but now that the ice has melted they cant do that anymore. because of this polar bears could one day become extinct, it's not just polar bears being affected by this issue. A lot of wildlife has had to change the way they live. 

The second reason we should all care about climate change is the weather. Every year the weather gets warmer and hotter, even in places where it's usually colder. This is called "the greenhouse effect". Since the earth is getting warmer, it's causing the ice in places where the weather is always cold to melt. It's very important to talk and raise awareness about climate change because of this. if we don't find a way to help, the earth is going to get warmer to a point where it's unbearable and it won't snow or get cold anymore.

the third reason is the earth. Climate change is destroying our world. It is destroying our waters, our forests, our animals and so much more. And the things that we are doing are not helping. The gas that is released into the air when people drive cars is contributing towards air pollution. The trash we throw into the oceans is causing water pollution which is killing sea creatures. It does not take much to do our part to help. Even the tiniest things matter, such as using less plastic cups and straws, putting trash in the right bins or biking every once in a while instead of driving all help us do our part to contribute towards slowing down climate change.

In conclusion, Climate change is a very important issue we should all care and raise awareness about. one of the reasons why is because of the way that it has destroyed the way animals have lived for millions of years. Another reason is because Climate change warms up our planets much hotter then it should be causing places that are colder like antartica to melt. Lastly because of the way that climate change destroys the planet we live in, in general. This is why everyone should care about climate change.
